title: SMART Scholarship-for-Service Program
legacy_titles: Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Scholarship-for-Service Program
program_type: National government scholarship-for-service administered by a federal department (scholarship in exchange for a fixed period of civilian employment)
funding_type: Competitive government scholarship: full tuition plus annual stipend, book and health allowances, and guaranteed post-graduation civilian employment, in exchange for a binding one-for-one service obligation
administering_authority: U.S. Department of War (DoW) (formerly the Department of Defense), Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Program Office, sponsored by the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering
implementing_agency: SMART Program Office (Department of War). Day-to-day programme administration and payment processing are performed under contract by the Logistics Management Institute (LMI), Scholarship America, iTechAG and Ernst & Young L.L.P. under a five-year cooperative agreement of up to USD 450,000,000 in total value; Scholarship America pays tuition and approved educational fees directly to the institution and stipends directly to recruitment scholars.
programme_action: Scholarship-for-Service programme under Title 10 U.S.C. 4093, funded through the National Defense Education Program and executed under DoDI 1025.09
description: The Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Scholarship-for-Service Program is a federal scholarship funded by the U.S. Department of War that awards full tuition, an annual stipend, health and book allowances, and paid summer internships at War Sponsoring Facilities to students pursuing STEM degrees. It is the largest education-to-workforce development initiative in the Department of War STEM portfolio and was established permanently by the 2006 National Defense Authorization Act after a 2005 pilot. Eligibility covers incoming college freshmen with no prior college credit, current undergraduates, and current War civilian employees, alongside master's and doctoral candidates. In exchange, each scholar accepts a binding one-for-one obligation of one year of War civilian employment for every year of funded degree study.

award_categories: Recruitment scholars — applicants who are not employed in a permanent War civilian position by a Sponsoring Facility at the time of award (the majority of awards)

Retention scholars — full-time permanent or renewable-term War civilian employees of a participating Sponsoring Facility at the time of award, who remain employed while pursuing the funded degree and fulfil the service commitment there
programme_structure.award_types_detail: Bachelor (BS) scholars: minimum 1.0 year and maximum 5.0 years of degree funding. Dual BS/MS scholars: minimum 1.0 year and maximum 5.0 years total, with both degrees in SMART approved STEM disciplines. Master (MS) scholars: minimum 1.0 year and maximum 3.0 years. Doctoral scholars: minimum 1.0 year and maximum 5.0 years. Each academic year funded obligates one full calendar year of Department of War civilian employment; funding that extends beyond a typical academic year is counted in 0.5 calendar year increments, and a partial academic year of support adds six months to the service commitment.
programme_structure.allocation: Annual national competition. Applications open 1 August and close 5:00 p.m. EST on the first Friday in December each year; the 2026 cycle closes 4 December 2026. Each Sponsoring Facility independently selects candidates against its own workforce needs, so no fixed allocation is published.
programme_structure.host_institutions: Any regionally accredited U.S. college or university, including regionally accredited online institutions. Some disciplines may additionally require ABET accreditation of the programme.
programme_structure.funding_years: Between 1 and 5 years of degree funding, with funding beginning in August of the year following the application cycle (August 2027 for the 2026 cycle).

verification_notes: Every figure, date and rule in this record was taken from the official SMART Scholarship site and the official 2026 SMART Scholar Handbook. Two points require explicit disclosure. First, the domain named in the research brief (smartscholarships.org) does not resolve in DNS; the official domain is smartscholarship.org (singular), which is the domain cited by the official government release as well. Second, the brief directed the researcher to verify that the award is restricted to U.S. citizens only. That is incorrect: the published eligibility list requires citizenship of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, or the United Kingdom, and the FAQ states that permanent residents are not eligible. This record corrects that claim rather than repeating it.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Annually from 1 August to the first Friday in December.
application_deadline.application_period: The 2026 cycle: registration and application open on 1 August 2026 and the online application must be submitted by 5:00 p.m. EST on Friday 4 December 2026, the first Friday in December. Registration is available only during the application cycle. Funded study begins 1 August 2027 and the estimated graduation date must be Spring 2028 or later.
application_deadline.official_rule: Official wording, Application Instructions page: 'Applications for the SMART Program are accepted annually, from August to December. Be sure to submit your online application by 5:00 p.m. EST on the first Friday in December, as late applications or reference submissions will not be accepted. Supporting materials, such as reference forms, must also be submitted by the deadline.' The About page states: 'The SMART Scholarship application is open annually beginning August 1 and closes the first Friday in December.' The Application Process FAQ states: 'The application cycle opens annually on August 1 and closes on the first Friday in December.' Because the official rule names a fixed month-day and clock time rather than a dated calendar deadline, the calendar date is derived from that rule for the current cycle: the first Friday in December 2026 is 4 December 2026, giving deadline_date 2026-12-04 and deadline_precision 'exact'. The live countdown rendered in the header of every official page read 55 days, 6 hours, 51 minutes on 2026-10-10 and therefore expires at 2026-12-04 at approximately 16:58 EST, confirming both the date and the 5:00 p.m. Eastern time.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Late applications and late reference submissions are not accepted, so the reference forms must be completed and received before the deadline. The 'Submit Application' button must be clicked before 5:00 p.m. EST on 4 December 2026 for the application to be considered; a saved but unsubmitted application does not count. Registration itself is only available while the cycle is open, so an applicant who has not registered cannot create an account after the deadline. Applicants should use Chrome on a desktop or laptop computer, since the site states that mobile use can cause technical issues.

programme_duration.official_range: A SMART award runs for the requested number of years of degree funding: bachelor (BS) scholars may request a minimum of 1.0 year and a maximum of 5.0 years. Each academic year funded obligates one full calendar year of Department of War civilian employment, so a 4-year bachelor's award carries a 48-month service commitment and the award-year band for BS scholars is 12 to 60 months of obligation. The SMART programme year runs from 1 August to 31 July.
programme_duration.renewal_note: A SMART award is not renewed year to year; it is granted for the requested award length and stated on the SMART Service Agreement. Continuation within the award requires full-time enrolment (unless otherwise approved) and a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, and an award may be rescinded if the GPA falls below 3.0 between application and award start or if awardee transcripts are not submitted by the 1 July deadline. A follow-on award for a further degree requires a new SMART application and fresh selection by the Sponsoring Facility and is not guaranteed; the maximum award length is 5.0 calendar years per award.

funding.scholarship_type: Government scholarship-for-service: full tuition and fees plus an annual stipend, health and book allowances, paid summer internships, and guaranteed post-graduation Department of War civilian employment, conditional on a binding one-for-one service obligation
funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly dollar amount is published. The official site publishes the stipend as an annual band — "Annual stipends range from $30,000 to $46,000 depending on your degree level" — and does not break the band down by degree level, so no bachelor-specific monthly figure can be stated. Recruitment scholars generally receive the stipend by monthly direct deposit on the third Friday of each month from August of the first award year, through Scholarship America; retention scholars receive it through their employing facility payroll system, where taxes are withheld.
funding.travel_amount_note: Internship Support Payments (ISPs) are available in addition to the monthly stipend to eligible recruitment scholars whose internship requires travel of 50 miles or more from their summer address. The payment is based on internship length and is capped at 12 weeks, and it is intended for travel, lodging, meals, transportation and incidental expenses. No dollar amount is published, so travel_amount is null. No relocation allowance is published for the post-graduation move, and the official guidance states that Sponsoring Facilities are usually not able to provide relocation costs, so scholars should expect to pay relocation and travel themselves.
funding.institutional_costs: The full cost of full-time tuition and approved related educational fees at any regionally accredited U.S. college or university is paid directly to the institution by Scholarship America on receipt of an invoice, using a sponsor letter issued to the scholar for the bursar. There is no cap on tuition and the amount of tuition does not affect the length of the service commitment. Full-time tuition covers the fall, winter and spring standard terms only; tuition for summer terms is not funded, and additional tuition or enrolment outside the standard academic year requires a Service Agreement Amendment Request.
funding.fully_funded_note: Tuition, fees, the stipend and the health and book allowances are fully covered, but the award is a scholarship-for-service with a binding one-for-one employment obligation and substantial conditions (security clearance, full-time enrolment, a 3.0 GPA, mandatory summer internships, and reimbursement of all funds on default), so it is not recorded as unconditionally fully funded. Deductible costs that remain with the scholar include federal, state and local taxes on the stipend (taxes are not withheld for recruitment scholars), summer-term tuition, and relocation to the Sponsoring Facility. The official site publishes no total programme value and none is computed here.

tuition.conditions: Full cost of full-time tuition and approved related educational fees at any regionally accredited U.S. college or university, paid directly to the institution by Scholarship America. No cap on tuition. Fall, winter and spring standard terms only; summer-term tuition is not funded and requires a separate approved SAAR.

monthly_stipend.annual_published_range: $30,000 to $46,000 per year depending on degree level
monthly_stipend.conditions: Annual stipend published only as a range ("between $30,000-$46,000 depending on degree level"); no degree-level breakdown is published, so the bachelor rate cannot be stated. Paid monthly to recruitment scholars by Scholarship America on the third Friday of each month from August of the first award year, pro-rated for partial academic years. Retention scholars are paid through their facility payroll with taxes withheld. Taxes are not withheld from recruitment stipends and are the scholar's responsibility.

travel_allowance.conditions: Internship Support Payments for eligible recruitment scholars travelling 50 miles or more to the Sponsoring Facility internship, covering travel, lodging, meals, transportation and incidentals. Amount is based on internship length and capped at 12 weeks. No post-graduation relocation allowance is published and facilities are usually unable to provide relocation costs.

installation_allowance.note: Not published in the official source. No relocation, settling-in or installation payment is offered; scholars are told to anticipate paying relocation and travel to the Sponsoring Facility themselves.

visa_support.note: Not published in the official source. SMART funds no visa or immigration costs, although United States citizen applicants are not affected.

insurance.conditions: An annual health insurance allowance is provided to recruitment scholars pro-rated for partial academic years. The handbook describes it as supplementing health insurance expenses; no dollar figure is published.

research_allowance.note: Not part of the standard bachelor award. SMART Innovation Awards and the SMART Scholar SEED Grant exist as separate competitive opportunities for scholars; the SEED grant was announced for Ph.D. scholars at up to USD 100,000 per year for a maximum of three years. None is published as part of the bachelor's award package, so it is not credited here.

book_allowance.conditions: An annual miscellaneous supplies allowance is provided for books, technology purchases and other school supplies, pro-rated for partial academic years. The programme materials describe this as a "Book & Health Allowance". No dollar figure is published.

equipment_allowance.note: Not published in the official source. The miscellaneous supplies allowance may be used for technology purchases, but no separate equipment allowance is published.

family_allowance.note: Not published in the official source. No dependent, spousal or family allowance is offered.

accommodation_support.note: Not published as an accommodation grant. Lodging for an internship can be covered within Internship Support Payments where the scholar is eligible, but no housing allowance is published.

bond.conditions: A binding service obligation applies: one calendar year (12 months) of full-time Department of War civilian employment at the Sponsoring Facility for each academic year of SMART funding. Minimum 1.0 year and maximum 5.0 years for BS scholars. A partial academic year of funding adds six months to the obligation. Time spent in Phase 1 internships and summer work does not count toward the commitment. The obligation cannot be deferred, the scholar must be geographically mobile within the United States, and it is in addition to any other civil service obligation. Breach results in dismissal, default on the SMART Service Agreement and liability for prompt reimbursement of all funds expended by the U.S. Government.

total_estimated_value.note: No total programme value is published and none is computed here, in line with the schema rule that a total value must not be presented as an award. The only published monetary figures are the $30,000 to $46,000 annual stipend band and the statement that tuition itself is uncapped.

coverage: Full cost of full-time tuition and approved related educational fees at any regionally accredited U.S. college or university, with no cap on tuition
Annual stipend published as a band of USD 30,000 to USD 46,000 per year depending on degree level, paid monthly to recruitment scholars through Scholarship America
Annual health insurance allowance for recruitment scholars
Annual miscellaneous supplies allowance for books, technology and school supplies
Paid summer internships of 8 to 12 weeks at the Department of War Sponsoring Facility, with the monthly stipend continuing during the internship period
Internship Support Payments for eligible recruitment scholars whose internship requires travel of 50 miles or more, capped at 12 weeks
Guaranteed post-graduation civilian employment with the Department of War at the Sponsoring Facility, for one year per year of funded study
Assigned sponsor mentor at the Sponsoring Facility and a Scholar Coordinator as the programme point of contact
coverage_limitations: Tuition is funded for the fall, winter and spring standard terms only; tuition for summer terms is not funded and requires an approved Service Agreement Amendment Request.

Relocation to the Sponsoring Facility after graduation is generally not paid: the official guidance states Sponsoring Facilities are usually not able to provide relocation costs, so scholars should expect to pay relocation and travel themselves.
Stipend payments to recruitment scholars are reported on IRS Form 1099-MISC, taxes are not withheld, and the scholar is responsible for all federal, state and local tax obligations.

Internship Support Payments are conditional on the distance between the summer address and the Sponsoring Facility and are capped at 12 weeks, so internship travel and lodging costs are not fully covered for every scholar.

The exact benefit structure, stipend rate and any allowances may differ for each individual award, since the stipend annual rate is set by the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering and is published only as a degree-level band.

The award is a scholarship-for-service: it is conditional on the signed SMART Service Agreement, on obtaining and maintaining a DoW security clearance, on full-time enrolment, and on a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0, and failure to complete the commitment triggers reimbursement of all funds.
SMART sets no salary for the post-graduation employment period; all salary and benefit details are determined by the Sponsoring Facility, so post-graduation income is not guaranteed by the programme.
eligible_applicants: Incoming college freshmen with no prior college credit, including high school seniors who will be pursuing a bachelor's degree in Fall 2027 (eligibility was expanded to this group)
Current undergraduates at any year of study at a regionally accredited U.S. college or university
Associate degree students and joint BS/MS students, registered through the corresponding academic-status options
Current full-time permanent or renewable-term Department of War civilian employees of participating Sponsoring Facilities, who apply as Retention applicants
Applicants who have completed a high school diploma or GED and have not yet started college
Reserve and National Guard members; active-duty members must be separated or on terminal leave on or before 1 August 2027
final_year_condition: Final-year secondary-school students are eligible: eligibility was expanded to include incoming college freshmen with no prior college credit, and the official eligibility page states that high school seniors and incoming college freshmen who will be pursuing a bachelor's degree in Fall 2027 are eligible to apply. High school seniors and incoming freshmen upload their most recent or final high school transcript. Current undergraduates at any year are also eligible, and an applicant need not be enrolled at the time of application but must be enrolled in a regionally accredited U.S. college or university by the programme start date of 1 August 2027.
equivalent_degree_note: A high school diploma or GED is an acceptable secondary credential for an applicant entering a funded bachelor's degree: the registration form offers the academic-status options "Currently pursuing HS Diploma/GED" and "Completed HS Diploma/GED and have not started College", and the Application Process FAQ confirms that "High school seniors and Incoming Freshman should use their most recent/Final high school transcript". Applicants must also be citizens of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, or the United Kingdom.

age_limit.age_calculation_date: 2028-01-01 (the applicant must be 18 years of age or older by 1 January 2028, the January 1 following the 1 August 2027 award start date; 17-year-olds may apply)

eligibility.citizenship: Applicants must be citizens of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, or the United Kingdom. Permanent residents are not eligible, and the registration form restricts citizenship to those five countries. The award is not restricted to U.S. citizens alone, contrary to the assumption in the research brief.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No residence requirement is published, but the degree must be pursued at a regionally accredited U.S. college or university (including a regionally accredited online U.S. institution), and the scholar must be willing to relocate within the United States for internship periods, workplace sponsorship changes, and the post-graduation service commitment at the assigned Sponsoring Facility.
eligibility.age_limit: 18 years of age or older by 1 January 2028. Applicants who are 17 may apply provided they will be 18 by that date, and the registration form rejects applicants who will be under 18 by 1 January 2028. The Department of War states it does not speak to parents unless the applicant is under 18.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: No specific secondary credential beyond a high school diploma or GED is published. High school seniors and incoming college freshmen with no prior college credit are eligible, and use their most recent or final high school transcript.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, held and maintained from the time of submitting the application through award and degree completion. The applicant must be pursuing, or intend to pursue, a degree in one of the SMART STEM disciplines, must be requesting between 1 and 5 years of degree funding with funding beginning in August 2027, must have an estimated graduation date of Spring 2028 or later, and must be able to obtain and maintain a DoW security clearance. Full-time enrolment is required during study unless otherwise approved, and ABET accreditation may be required for applicable STEM disciplines.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: Cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, reported exactly as it appears on the current transcript (using a combined cumulative GPA where the transcript shows one), and maintained thereafter; the registration form rejects GPA values below 3.00.
eligibility.language_requirement: No English-language proficiency requirement is published by SMART. No IELTS, TOEFL, PTE or Duolingo score is required or considered. Because funded study takes place at a regionally accredited U.S. institution, that institution may impose its own English proficiency requirement at admission, which is separate from SMART.
eligibility.work_experience: No work experience is required. Retention applicants must already hold a full-time permanent or renewable-term Department of War civilian position with a participating Sponsoring Facility, and must supply a signed supervisor letter on official letterhead.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: No extracurricular requirement is published. The application contains a "My Experiences" section that applicants complete, but no minimum participation is stated.
eligibility.financial_need: Not a published criterion. SMART is described as a merit-based programme for STEM students and no financial-need test is stated.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Concurrent funding from the NDSEG Fellowship, the DoW Cyber Scholarship Program, AFCS Palace Acquire, the Barry Goldwater Scholarship and the NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program is prohibited. Current ROTC participants with a future service commitment are not eligible, and pre-existing service commitments from SSEP, Pathways or PCIP must be resolved. Private scholarships, fellowships, grants and loans, and certain Veterans Affairs education benefits, may be accepted.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: The applicant does not need to be enrolled at the time of application. Applicants must be pursuing, or intend to pursue, education in Fall 2027 and must be enrolled in a regionally accredited U.S. college or university by the programme start date of 1 August 2027, providing proof of enrolment before the award begins. Active-duty applicants must be separated or on terminal leave on or before 1 August 2027.
eligibility.health_requirement: No health or medical requirement is published. Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain the level of DoW security clearance required by their Sponsoring Facility, including interim and final clearance; clearance is initiated by the Sponsoring Facility after award and involves the SF-86 Questionnaire for National Security adjudicated under DoDM 5200.02. A failed prescreening can cause the award to be rescinded or sponsorship to be withdrawn.
eligibility.field_restrictions: The degree must fall under one of the SMART STEM disciplines published on the eligibility page: Aerospace and Aeronautical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Biosciences, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Civil Engineering, Cognitive, Neural, and Behavioral Sciences, Computer Science and Engineering, Data Science and Analytics, Electrical Engineering, Geosciences, Industrial and Systems Engineering, Information Sciences, Materials Science and Engineering, Mathematics, Mechanical Engineering, Naval Architecture and Ocean Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Oceanography, Operations Research, Physics, and Software Engineering. A major not explicitly listed is still eligible if it falls under a broader published discipline, for example statistics under mathematics. Non-technical degrees, including management, arts and humanities, are not approved or funded.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No fixed percentage, class rank or standardised-test threshold is required. The only quantitative academic threshold published is a cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. The FAQ states explicitly that "SAT, ACT, or GRE scores are not required and are not considered during evaluation".
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: The proposed degree must fall under one of the SMART STEM disciplines, with the applicant selecting the overarching discipline most aligned with their field on the application. The applicant must request between 1 and 5 years of degree funding, with funding beginning August 2027, and an estimated degree completion date of Spring 2028 or later. The proposed institution must be a regionally accredited U.S. college or university (undecided applicants may select "Undecided" or "Other (Not Listed)"). Bachelor scholars may be funded for a maximum of 5.0 years.
selection_factors_may_include: The strength of the undergraduate transcript against the 3.0 GPA minimum
Technical fit between the applicant's STEM discipline and the workforce needs of the chosen Sponsoring Facility, since each facility selects independently
The ranked Sponsoring Facility preferences, with a stated reason for each selection
The resume, the personal statement and the "My Experiences" section of the application
The submitted references from individuals familiar with the applicant's academic achievements or professional experience
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Selection is decentralised: participating Sponsoring Facilities independently review applications and select candidates based on their own workforce needs, rather than a central panel scoring a national pool. SMART states that individual selection feedback is not provided because each facility conducts its own evaluation, so no national weighting or cut-off score can be published.

english_requirement.test_score_note: SMART publishes no English-language proficiency requirement and accepts no language test scores for its own evaluation. Because funded study is at a regionally accredited U.S. institution in English, the admitting institution may set its own English proficiency requirement, which must be satisfied for admission but is separate from the SMART award.

language_of_instruction.language_note: All funded study is delivered in English at regionally accredited U.S. colleges and universities. SMART sets no language requirement of its own, though STEM disciplines such as foreign language instruction are outside the approved discipline list.

application_method.application_route: Online only, through the SMART application portal. The applicant first completes the registration form on the eligibility-check page during the application cycle; if eligible, SMART emails login credentials for the Application Portal, the applicant completes every section, and then clicks "Submit Application" before the deadline.
application_steps: 1. Read the Eligibility page and the list of SMART STEM disciplines and confirm citizenship of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand or the United Kingdom, age 18 or older by 1 January 2028, and a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
2. Research the Sponsoring Facilities and identify at least three, with up to five ranked preferences and a reason for each, since placement is determined by facility workforce needs.
3. Complete the SMART registration form during the 1 August to first-Friday-in-December cycle and click "Check My Eligibility", then "Submit Registration".
4. Receive login credentials by email, set up account authentication, and log in to the Application Portal.

5. Complete every section of the application: Privacy Act Statement, Application Instructions, Program Materials, Upload Resume, Upload Transcript, About Me, References, My Experiences, Proposed Award Details and Personal Statement.
6. Upload the most recent unofficial transcript (high school seniors and incoming freshmen upload their most recent or final high school transcript) and the resume.
7. Enter at least two and up to three references; each reference submits their own form, and all reference forms must be received by the deadline.
8. Enter Proposed Award Details: institution, degree level, estimated completion date, years of funding, current enrolment status and STEM discipline.
9. Write and submit the personal statement.
10. Click "Submit Application" before 5:00 p.m. EST on the first Friday in December and monitor application status to confirm all reference forms were received.

universal_documents: Completed online application with every section filled (Privacy Act Statement, Application Instructions, Program Materials, Upload Resume, Upload Transcript, About Me, References, My Experiences, Proposed Award Details, Personal Statement)
At least two completed reference forms (up to three references may be entered)
commonly_requested_documents: Ranked Sponsoring Facility preferences, at least three and up to five, with a reason given for each selection
Proposed Award Details covering proposed institution, degree level, estimated degree completion date, requested years of funding, current enrolment status and SMART STEM discipline
Signed Supervisor Letter on official letterhead, required only for Retention applicants who are current War civilian employees
official_application_documents.secondary_school_documents: High school seniors and incoming college freshmen upload their most recent or final high school transcript. Applicants who completed a high school diploma or GED and have not started college are eligible through a distinct academic-status option.
official_application_documents.document_language: Not specified by SMART. The application is completed and submitted in English.
official_application_documents.document_format: Electronic upload within the SMART Application Portal. No paper application is available and application materials are not returned to applicants.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Upload the most recent unofficial transcript. High school seniors and incoming freshmen should use their most recent or final high school transcript. Report the cumulative GPA exactly as it appears on the current transcript, using a combined cumulative GPA where the transcript includes one. Awardee transcripts are due by 1 July, and if grades for the degree to be funded fall below a cumulative 3.0 GPA between application and award start, or transcripts are not submitted by that deadline, the award may be rescinded.

identity_documents.document: Registration details including first, middle and last name, date of birth, email address and country of citizenship
identity_documents.notes: Collected through the SMART registration form, which uses the date of birth to test the minimum age of 18 by 1 January 2028. Email must be on a .edu, .com, .net, .org, .mil or .gov domain. No identity document upload is listed in the published application sections.

academic_documents.document: Most recent unofficial transcript (most recent or final high school transcript for high school seniors and incoming freshmen)
academic_documents.notes: Uploaded to the Upload Transcript section. Cumulative GPA must be reported exactly as it appears on the transcript. Awardee transcripts are additionally due by 1 July.
Uploaded to the Upload Resume section; the FAQ advises drafting and revising the resume and personal statement early in the 8-week application roadmap.

academic_documents.document: Proposed Award Details (institution, degree level, estimated completion date, years of funding, enrolment status, STEM discipline)
academic_documents.notes: The proposed institution must be a regionally accredited U.S. college or university; undecided applicants select "Undecided" or "Other (Not Listed)". The estimated completion date must be Spring 2028 or later for the 2026 cycle, and the requested years of funding auto-populate from it.

language_documents.notes: SMART requires and considers no English language test scores. The admitting U.S. institution may impose its own English proficiency requirement for admission, which is separate from the SMART application.

recommendation_documents.document: Reference forms, at least two and up to three
recommendation_documents.notes: Each reference submits their own task within the portal. References should be individuals familiar with the applicant's academic achievements or professional experience, preferably in STEM-related settings. All reference forms must be received before the deadline, since late reference submissions are not accepted, and references cannot be carried forward from a previous cycle.

application_essays.notes: Completed in the Personal Statement section of the portal. The application is not submittable until every section, including this one, is complete.

application_essays.document: About Me and My Experiences sections
application_essays.notes: Structured sections of the portal application covering the applicant's background and experiences; no separate essay upload is published.

financial_documents.document: No financial documentation required by SMART
financial_documents.notes: SMART is a merit-based programme with no financial-need test, so no financial documents are required. Scholarship America issues recruitment scholars an IRS Form 1099-MISC, taxes are not withheld, and the scholar is responsible for their own tax obligations.

additional_documents.notes: Required only for Retention applicants who are current full-time permanent or term civilian employees of a participating Sponsoring Facility. A signed letter on official letterhead describing the applicant's position, the supervisor relationship, a statement of support, and how the proposed degree benefits the facility.

additional_documents.document: Privacy Act Statement acknowledgement and Program Materials review
additional_documents.notes: These are sections of the portal application that must be completed before the "Submit Application" button appears.

additional_documents.document: Awardee-stage documents after selection (SMART Service Agreement, media release, spring transcripts, site visit report, orientation and onboarding paperwork)
additional_documents.notes: Required only after award, between the first-week-of-April notification and the 1 August start date, along with a 1-2 day Sponsoring Facility site visit for Recruitment awardees.

required_documents: Completed online application in the SMART Application Portal with every section complete (Privacy Act Statement, Application Instructions, Program Materials, Upload Resume, Upload Transcript, About Me, References, My Experiences, Proposed Award Details, Personal Statement)
Most recent unofficial transcript (most recent or final high school transcript for high school seniors and incoming freshmen)
At least two completed reference forms (up to three references may be entered), submitted by the references themselves
Ranked Sponsoring Facility preferences: at least three and up to five, each with a stated reason
Proposed Award Details: proposed institution, degree level, estimated completion date, requested years of funding, current enrolment status and SMART STEM discipline
Signed Supervisor Letter on official letterhead (Retention applicants only)
SMART Service Agreement and media release (after award)

selection_process.decision_maker: Each participating Sponsoring Facility, that is a Department of War laboratory, agency or organisation within one of the four sponsoring components (Army, Navy, Air Force, and Other War Agencies), independently reviews applications and selects candidates. The SMART Program Office sets policy and oversight; it does not select awardees, and SMART states that individual selection feedback is not provided because each facility conducts its own evaluation.
selection_process.selection_type: Competitive decentralised selection by Sponsoring Facilities based on their own workforce needs, following a central application
possible_stages: Registration and eligibility screen during the 1 August to first-Friday-in-December cycle
Online application submitted with transcript, resume, personal statement, Proposed Award Details and at least two reference forms
Evaluation by the ranked Sponsoring Facilities from January to March, including facility interviews
Award notification in the first week of April
Award acceptance, SMART Service Agreement signing, site visit and site visit report for Recruitment awardees
Background check and security clearance prescreening conducted by the Sponsoring Facility
July orientation and onboarding call, with awardee transcripts due by 1 July
Award start on 1 August and funded study beginning in the Fall term
selection_process.weighting_note: No universal weighting is published. Selection is made independently by each Sponsoring Facility against its own workforce needs, and SMART publishes no scoring model, cut-off or weightings, so any weighting would have to be programme-specific rather than national.
selection_process.results_timing: Applications are evaluated and Sponsoring Facilities conduct interviews from January to March. Award recipients are notified in the first week of April, and unfortunately unsuccessful applicants are given no individual feedback.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: Applicants must select at least three sponsoring facilities and may list up to five preferences, each with a stated reason. Preference is considered, but placement with a Sponsoring Facility is determined by the needs of the Department of War and by the selecting facility, and the scholar is told the facility and location at the time of award. Applicants may decline an offer, but declining forfeits the award and requires reapplying.

additional_factors: Technical fit with the workforce needs of the chosen Sponsoring Facility, since each facility selects independently
The ranked Sponsoring Facility preferences and the reason given for each selection
Strength of the resume, personal statement and "My Experiences" section
Quality of the reference forms from individuals familiar with the applicant's academic or professional STEM experience
Ability to obtain and maintain the DoW security clearance required by the facility

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: A bachelor's degree in a SMART STEM discipline conferred by the regionally accredited U.S. college or university at which the scholar is enrolled. SMART is a funding and employment programme, not a degree-awarding body.
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Four years for a full-time bachelor's degree in the United States. SMART funds bachelor scholars for between 1 and 5 years depending on the award requested.
possible_awards: Bachelor (BS) degree in a SMART STEM discipline, funded for 1.0 to 5.0 years
Dual BS/MS award, funding both degrees where both are in SMART approved STEM disciplines, for a combined maximum of 5.0 years
degree_outcome.degree_note: The scholar must be enrolled full time unless otherwise approved and must maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Changes of institution or major may require SMART approval through a Service Agreement Amendment Request, and the award may be amended if the degree completion date crosses from one programme year to the next, adding 0.5 years to both the award and the service commitment. A separate follow-on application and re-selection is required for any further degree such as a Ph.D.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Full cost of full-time tuition and approved related educational fees is paid directly to the institution by Scholarship America against an invoice, using a sponsor letter provided to the bursar. There is no cap on tuition and the amount of tuition does not affect the length of the service commitment. Summer-term tuition is excluded.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: SMART publishes no application fee for the scholarship, and no fee waiver mechanism is published. Any application fee is set separately by the admitting college or university.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: The SMART Service Agreement (SSA), a formal binding written agreement between the scholar and the Department of War which the scholar signs to accept the award and which obligates compliance with all programme policies and the SMART Scholar Handbook. If an SSA is signed while the scholar is a minor it must also be co-signed by a parent or legal guardian, and on reaching 18 the scholar must sign the SSA again to reaffirm the terms. Amendments are made only through Service Agreement Amendment Requests approved by the Component Execution Lead.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: A Scholar Coordinator assigned as the first point of contact during degree pursuit; a designated mentor within the Sponsoring Facility who facilitates internship arrangements and provides one-to-one counselling on agency operations; summer internship placement; a 1-2 day Recruitment awardee site visit with a site visit report; July orientation and an onboarding call; and access to international internship opportunities, Innovation Awards and the Ambassador Program. Recipients may also accept private scholarships, fellowships, grants and loans alongside the award.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: A binding one-for-one service commitment applies. Each academic year of SMART funding obligates one calendar year (12 months) of full-time civilian employment with the Department of War at the Sponsoring Facility, with a minimum of 1.0 year and a maximum of 5.0 years for bachelor scholars. Support for a partial academic year adds six months to the commitment. Time spent in Phase 1 internships and summer work does not count toward it. The commitment is in addition to any other civil service obligation, cannot be deferred, and requires the scholar to be willing to relocate within the United States.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: Failure to complete the post-graduation service commitment results in dismissal from the SMART Program, default on the SMART Service Agreement and liability for prompt reimbursement of any and all funds expended under the programme by the U.S. Government, with debt established by the Component Execution Lead. Voluntary withdrawal after 1 August of the first award year is likewise a default. The award may also be rescinded or sponsorship withdrawn if the scholar fails the security clearance prescreening, falls below a cumulative 3.0 GPA, or does not submit awardee transcripts by the 1 July deadline. There is no debt-relief mechanism published for declining an offer before the start date, since declining before then simply forfeits the award.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm citizenship of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand or the United Kingdom (permanent residents are not eligible) and that you will be 18 or older by 1 January 2028
Confirm your cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale is at least 3.00 as it appears on your most recent transcript
Confirm your intended major falls under one of the SMART STEM disciplines, and check the qualifying-majors list if it is not explicitly named
Confirm your estimated graduation date is Spring 2028 or later and decide how many years of funding (1 to 5) you need
Identify and rank at least three, and up to five, Sponsoring Facilities, and write a reason for each, since placement is driven by facility workforce needs
Request reference forms early from at least two people familiar with your academic or professional STEM work; all forms must arrive before the deadline
Draft, revise and finalise the resume and personal statement using the published 8-week application roadmap
Prepare the most recent unofficial transcript (or your final high school transcript if you are a high school senior or incoming freshman) for upload
Register on the SMART registration page while the cycle is open, since registration is not available outside the cycle

On a desktop or laptop in Chrome, complete every portal section and click "Submit Application" well before 5:00 p.m. EST on the first Friday in December, then monitor status to confirm references were received
programme_comparison_fields: Award value: full tuition (uncapped) plus a USD 30,000 to USD 46,000 annual stipend band, plus health and book allowances
Monetary conditionality: binding service obligation of one year of DoW civilian employment per year of funding, 1 to 5 years for bachelor scholars
Career outcome: guaranteed civilian employment at a War Sponsoring Facility, with salary set by the facility under OPM guidance rather than by SMART
Selection model: decentralised selection by individual Sponsoring Facilities rather than a central national panel
Academic threshold: cumulative GPA 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, with no SAT, ACT or GRE requirement
Citizenship: United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand or United Kingdom citizens only
Intake point: incoming college freshmen with no prior college credit are eligible, unlike most undergraduate scholarships
Non-monetary conditions: security clearance, full-time enrolment, mandatory 8-12 week summer internships for multi-year awards, and geographic mobility within the United States
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: Write the personal statement around the specific technical mission of the ranked Sponsoring Facilities, because selection is made by each facility against its own workforce needs rather than by a central panel. State the SMART STEM discipline you will pursue and map it to one of the published critical technology areas such as Applied Artificial Intelligence, Biomanufacturing, Contested Logistics Technologies, Quantum and Battlefield Information Dominance, Scaled Directed Energy or Scaled Hypersonics, and explain concretely how your degree and internship work would contribute. Address the service commitment head-on: confirm that you accept a one-for-one obligation, that you are willing to relocate within the United States, and that you can obtain and maintain a security clearance. Keep each stated facility preference distinct and give a real reason for it, since applicants must rank at least three facilities and placement follows facility need. Because no test scores are considered, let the transcript, resume, references and the My Experiences section carry the academic and technical evidence.
profile_fit_labels: High-achieving U.S., Australian, Canadian, New Zealand or British citizen entering a bachelor's degree in Fall 2027 with at least a 3.0 GPA
Current undergraduate already in a STEM degree at a regionally accredited U.S. institution
Current DoW civilian employee seeking part-time or full-time degree funding through a Retention award
Applicant who wants a guaranteed civilian career path at a national laboratory or defence facility
Applicant comfortable with a multi-year post-graduation employment commitment and relocation within the United States
Applicant eligible and willing to obtain a U.S. security clearance
common_mistakes: Assuming the award is restricted to U.S. citizens: Australia, Canada, New Zealand and United Kingdom citizens are also eligible
Assuming an SAT, ACT or GRE score is needed: the FAQ states standardised test scores are not required and are not considered
Submitting the application without clicking "Submit Application": a saved but unsubmitted application is not considered, and the button only appears once every section is complete
Assuming references can be added after the deadline: late reference submissions are not accepted, so all reference forms must arrive before the deadline
Listing only one or two Sponsoring Facilities: at least three must be selected and up to five may be ranked, each with a stated reason
Reusing a previous cycle's application: previous applications and references are not carried forward and cannot be reactivated
Negotiating salary with SMART: the programme does not set Phase 2 salaries and informal discussions do not constitute an offer
Assuming the summer internship counts toward the service commitment: internship time in Phase 1 is not credited
Assuming summer-term tuition is covered: only fall, winter and spring standard terms are funded
Waiting to apply near the deadline: registration is only available while the cycle is open, so an unregistered applicant cannot create an account afterwards

risk_flags.risk: A binding one-for-one service obligation of one year of Department of War civilian employment per year of funded study, of up to five years for a bachelor scholar, applies after graduation
risk_flags.impact: The scholar is contractually tied to a single Sponsoring Facility for years after graduation, cannot defer the employment period, and must be geographically mobile within the United States
risk_flags.mitigation: Research the Sponsoring Facility, its location and its mission before ranking preferences, and contact the facility before accepting the award to confirm the placement is compatible

risk_flags.risk: Failure to complete the service commitment triggers dismissal and liability for prompt reimbursement of all funds expended by the U.S. Government
risk_flags.impact: A default could create a substantial debt equal to every dollar of tuition, stipend and allowances the programme paid, with debt established by the Component Execution Lead
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the award as a contractual obligation rather than a grant, and confirm the ability to complete the degree, obtain the clearance and serve the full period before accepting

risk_flags.risk: A DoW security clearance is required, initiated by the Sponsoring Facility after award and adjudicated under DoDM 5200.02, including an SF-86
risk_flags.impact: If the prescreening does not recommend interim clearance during Phase 0 the award may be rescinded, and during Phase 1 the facility may withdraw sponsorship, which can lead to dismissal
risk_flags.mitigation: Disclose background history completely and early, provide requested documentation promptly, and notify the facility before foreign travel as the handbook requires

risk_flags.risk: Selection is decentralised: each Sponsoring Facility independently selects candidates against its own workforce needs, and SMART gives no individual feedback
risk_flags.impact: A strong GPA does not guarantee selection, and an applicant may be rejected for reasons specific to a facility's staffing needs with no explanation available
risk_flags.mitigation: Rank multiple facilities with genuine reasons, align the field of study with each facility's technical mission, and reapply in a later cycle, since reapplying is explicitly encouraged

risk_flags.risk: The stipend is published only as a band of USD 30,000 to USD 46,000 per year depending on degree level, with no degree-level breakdown and no cap on tuition
risk_flags.impact: The exact bachelor-level stipend cannot be known in advance, so the real disposable income during study is uncertain, and taxes are not withheld from recruitment stipends
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget for the tax liability on the stipend yourself, consult a tax professional, and ask the SMART Program Office or the Sponsoring Facility for the current bachelor stipend rate before accepting

risk_flags.risk: Relocation costs for the post-graduation move are generally not covered, since Sponsoring Facilities are usually unable to provide relocation costs
risk_flags.impact: The scholar must fund travel and relocation to the Sponsoring Facility personally, immediately upon graduation and before or at the start of employment
risk_flags.mitigation: Save from the stipend during the funded period and confirm salary, benefits and relocation terms directly with the facility during Phase 1, remembering that informal discussions are not an offer

risk_flags.risk: The award requires full-time enrolment, a maintained cumulative 3.0 GPA, and mandatory summer internships of 8 to 12 weeks for awards of more than about 1.5 years
risk_flags.impact: A drop below 3.0 GPA, incomplete coursework, loss of full-time status or failure to submit transcripts by 1 July can lead to non-compliance, dismissal and debt
risk_flags.mitigation: Plan the degree so coursework and the internship can both be completed in the funded years, and submit spring transcripts promptly when requested

risk_flags.risk: Concurrent funding from certain federal programmes is prohibited, including the NDSEG Fellowship, the DoW Cyber Scholarship Program, AFCS Palace Acquire, the Barry Goldwater Scholarship and the NSF GRFP
risk_flags.impact: Holding one of those awards alongside a SMART award would breach the programme rules
risk_flags.mitigation: Check any other federal scholarship or fellowship held or planned, and resolve any pre-existing SSEP, Pathways or PCIP service commitment or debt before accepting

image.logo_verification_method: The asset is served from the official awarding body's own domain, www.smartscholarship.org, and is declared by that domain as the programme's social share image: the official homepage HTML contains <meta name="twitter:image" content="https://www.smartscholarship.org/social_logo.png"> and an equivalent og:image declaration. The URL was requested directly and returned HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/png;charset=UTF-8 and a size of 17,964 bytes. The file was downloaded and decoded: it is a 207 by 195 pixel 8-bit RGBA PNG carrying Adobe XMP metadata. The rendered image is the SMART logo lockup reading "SMART / SCIENCE, MATHEMATICS, AND RESEARCH FOR TRANSFORMATION / PART OF THE NATIONAL DEFENSE EDUCATION PROGRAM", which is the programme's own wordmark rather than a photograph, stock image or third-party aggregator copy.
image.image_usage_note: No photograph is recorded. The official homepage and eligibility page use photographs of scholars and students, but no individual image is published as an official branded asset, so none is asserted here.

official_fields_confirmed: Official award name: Science, Mathematics, and Research for Transformation (SMART) Scholarship-for-Service Program

Current administering department name: the U.S. Department of War (DoW), with the site header reading "Department of War (DoW) Scholarship-for-Service Program" and the handbook naming the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering as sponsor with delegated authority to the ASD(S&T), the DoW Basic Research Office and the SMART Program Office

Legal and policy basis: established pursuant to Title 10 U.S.C. 4093 and funded through the National Defense Education Program under DoDI 1025.09; permanently established by the 2006 National Defense Authorization Act after a 2005 pilot

Statutory benefit: full cost of full-time tuition and approved related educational fees at any regionally accredited U.S. college or university, paid directly to the institution by Scholarship America, with no cap on tuition

Annual stipend published as a band of USD 30,000 to USD 46,000 depending on degree level, paid monthly to recruitment scholars by Scholarship America on the third Friday of each month from August of the first award year
Annual health insurance allowance and annual miscellaneous supplies (book and technology) allowance for recruitment scholars

Summer internships of 8 to 12 weeks at the DoW Sponsoring Facility, not separately paid but with the monthly stipend continuing, plus Internship Support Payments for scholars travelling 50 miles or more capped at 12 weeks

Post-graduation service obligation: one calendar year (12 months) of full-time DoW civilian employment per academic year of funding, minimum 1.0 year and maximum 5.0 years for bachelor scholars; a partial academic year adds six months; internship time does not count
Service agreement enforcement: dismissal, SSA default and prompt reimbursement of all funds if the commitment is not completed; withdrawal after 1 August of the first award year is a default

Post-graduation salary basis: set by the Sponsoring Facility under Office of Personnel Management guidance, not by SMART, with informal Phase 1 discussions not constituting an offer and relocation costs usually not provided
Citizenship: citizens of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand or the United Kingdom only; permanent residents are not eligible
Minimum age: 18 or older by 1 January 2028, with 17-year-olds permitted if they reach 18 by that date
GPA threshold: cumulative 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, held from application through award and degree; awardee transcripts due by 1 July
Incoming college freshmen with no prior college credit, including high school seniors, are eligible, and need not be enrolled at application but must be enrolled by the 1 August 2027 start date
Funding window: 1 to 5 years of degree funding requested, funding beginning August 2027, estimated graduation Spring 2028 or later
Award lengths: bachelor scholars 1.0 to 5.0 years, master's 1.0 to 3.0 years, dual BS/MS and doctoral 1.0 to 5.0 years
No SAT, ACT or GRE scores are required or considered
Security clearance requirement, initiated by the Sponsoring Facility after award and adjudicated under DoDM 5200.02 via the SF-86
22 SMART STEM disciplines published on the eligibility page, with non-technical degrees such as management, arts and humanities explicitly not funded

Application cycle: opens annually 1 August and closes 5:00 p.m. EST on the first Friday in December; late applications and late reference submissions are not accepted; registration only available during the cycle
Exact calendar deadline for the current cycle: 4 December 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST, confirmed by the live on-site countdown resolving to 2026-12-04 at approximately 16:58 EST

Required documents and portal sections, including most recent unofficial transcript (final high school transcript for seniors), resume, personal statement, at least two and up to three references, ranked Sponsoring Facility preferences of at least three and up to five, and the Retention supervisor letter

Selection model: decentralised, with each Sponsoring Facility independently reviewing and selecting against its own workforce needs, conducting interviews from January to March, and no individual feedback provided
Notification timing: award recipients notified in the first week of April; results timing in the spring
Programme scale: 202 mission-critical Sponsoring Facilities, 6,510 scholarships awarded to date, and a 91% successful completion rate of the service commitment
No application fee and no paper application: all applications must be submitted online
Prohibited concurrent funding: NDSEG, DoW Cyber Scholarship Program, AFCS Palace Acquire, Barry Goldwater Scholarship and NSF GRFP; current ROTC participants with a future commitment are ineligible
Official logo asset URL on the programme's own domain, its HTTP 200 availability and its 207 by 195 pixel PNG structure

database_notes: PREVIOUS-AWARD RESTRICTIONS: applicants may apply more than once and are encouraged to reapply if not selected, but a new application must be submitted each cycle and previous applications and references are not carried forward. Recipients may not concurrently receive funding from the NDSEG Fellowship, the DoW Cyber Scholarship Program, AFCS Palace Acquire, the Barry Goldwater Scholarship or the NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program; private scholarships, fellowships, grants and loans are permitted, and certain Veterans Affairs education benefits may be used in limited circumstances. Current ROTC participants with a future service commitment are not eligible, and a scholar whose selection triggers a pre-existing service commitment through SSEP, Pathways or PCIP must resign and resolve that commitment or debt. This content is recorded here rather than as an extra top-level key because the schema contract permits additional keys only inside open maps.

DOMAIN CORRECTION: the brief named smartscholarships.org (plural). That host does not resolve in DNS — Resolve-DnsName returns only an SOA record and the browser reports ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED. The official domain is smartscholarship.org (singular), which is also the domain cited in the official government release. All research was performed on the singular domain.

CITIZENSHIP CORRECTION: the brief asked the researcher to verify that the award is U.S.-citizens only. The official eligibility page states "Be a citizen of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, or United Kingdom", and the registration form restricts the citizenship question to exactly those five countries plus "None of the Above". The FAQ adds that permanent residents are not eligible. The record therefore sets citizenship_restriction true and worldwide_eligibility false, but records five eligible nationalities rather than one.

DEPARTMENT NAMING: the awarding department is currently the U.S. Department of War (DoW), previously the Department of Defense. The programme site header reads "Department of War (DoW) Scholarship-for-Service Program" and the pages refer to funder, facilities and careers as DoW. The official government site war.gov (the successor domain to defense.gov) still carries "U.S. Department of War" branding while some article bodies still say DoD, and the 2026 SMART Scholar Handbook still uses the legacy abbreviation USD(R&E) alongside the current Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering (USW(R&E)). Both forms are recorded so the record survives either naming.

STIPEND: the official site publishes the stipend only as a degree-level band, "Annual stipends range from $30,000 to $46,000 depending on your degree level" (and on the homepage, "SMART scholars earn annual stipends between $30,000-$46,000 depending on degree level"). The 2026 Scholar Handbook confirms only that scholars "receive a stipend based on an annual rate as determined by USD(R&E)" without publishing the rate. No bachelor-specific figure exists on the official site, so no single dollar figure is asserted and none is estimated.

DEADLINE: the official rule is "5:00 p.m. EST on the first Friday in December" rather than a printed calendar date. The first Friday in December 2026 is 4 December 2026, which is recorded as the exact date. The live countdown published in the header of every official page read 55 days, 6 hours and 51 minutes remaining when it was read on 2026-10-10 and therefore expires at 2026-12-04 at approximately 16:58 EST, independently confirming both the date and the 5:00 p.m. Eastern time. The site's own wording uses "EST"; December in the U.S. Eastern zone is standard time (UTC-5), so EST and ET are equivalent for this date.

SERVICE OBLIGATION: the programme describes the obligation both as "one-for-one" and as "a one-to-one commitment", defined in the glossary FAQ as one year (12 months) of civilian employment per academic year of funding. The handbook adds the arithmetic: 1.5 academic years requires 18 months, 2.0 academic years requires 24 months, and partial academic years add six months. The handbook also states that time spent in Phase 1 internships does not count toward the commitment.

FULLY FUNDED: because the award carries a binding service obligation and reimbursement-on-default exposure, fully_funded is recorded as false in line with the schema rule that a scholarship with a service bond must never be presented as unconditionally fully funded. The scholarship_currency and monthly_amount fields hold real nulls, not the string "null".

SCOPE: the award also funds master's and doctoral STEM degrees. This record is the bachelor's-level record as assigned, and the higher-level coverage is noted in funding_breakdown, programme_structure and degree_outcome rather than being omitted.

STATUS: the cycle is OPEN as of 2026-10-10, with the deadline on 2026-12-04 still in the future. Funding for this cohort begins 1 August 2027, with award notifications in the first week of April 2027.

VERIFICATION DATE: the schema contract gives a reference date of 2026-10-03. The official pages and the 2026 Scholar Handbook were actually read on 2026-10-10, and the live deadline countdown read on that date resolves to 4 December 2026, so last_verified_date, last_verified_at, _verification_timestamp, logo_verified_at and image_verified_at are recorded as 2026-10-10 rather than the contract's illustrative reference date. Using 2026-10-03 would misstate when the pages were read.

SOURCE LAST UPDATED: no page-level last-updated date is published, so source_last_updated is null.
